notes:
Summary: mid-market sales enablement SaaS building outbound SDR chat agents to automate prospect outreach and calendar scheduling. Currently prototyping streaming chat agents that do: parse reply intent, call internal CRM (write lead status), send personalized email, propose calendar times and create invites via API.

Key constraints / asks: streaming p95 < 300ms for single-turn replies; tool-calls must be low-latency (CRM write in <300-500ms ideally); support for real-time streaming partial tokens for UX. Looking at hosted API for quick POC, long-term likely Dedicated for predictable peak throughput and data isolation (customer data).

What we did on call: Marco ran synthetic load test during demo — at 50 concurrent agents streaming we started to see tail latency spikes; AE noted business requirement = 200 rps peak during morning outbound windows. Team wants suggestions on batching, token limits, and whether prefix caching could help for templated content.

Security feedback: require SSO/SAML, audit logs for user actions, option for customer-managed KMS, and EU residency for subset of customer data. Legal asked for SOC2 attestation and breach notification SLA.

Pricing/contract: VP Rev asked for committed Dedicated pricing vs hosted per-token for 12-month commit. Concern about token cost with high outbound volume. "If tokens are the killer, we'll eat the latency but not the bill" — VP Rev.

Next steps (short): run 2-week hosted POC (Redwood to provide sample dashboard for p95/p50 token cost), run focused load test simulating 200 rps with streaming and tool calling, Redwood SE to draft Dedicated sizing and 12-mo commit pricing.

Staging notes: moving from evaluation -> procurement depends on POC outcomes and pricing.
